An object is projected horizontally from a table at time t = 0. The object falls in a uniform
gravitational field. Air resistance is negligible.
Graphs P, Q, R and S are velocity–time graphs.

hints: Notice the starting values at $t = 0$: the object is projected horizontally, so horizontal $v$ starts at a non-zero value while vertical $v$ starts at zero.
Connect force to acceleration in each direction: with negligible air resistance there is no horizontal force but there is constant vertical weight, so think constant $v$ versus constant $a$.
Recall what constant acceleration looks like on a $v$-$t$ graph: a straight line with constant gradient, so compare straight-line-through-origin P with curved S for the vertical component.
walkthrough: Separate the motion: horizontally there is no force when air resistance is negligible, so horizontal acceleration is zero and horizontal velocity stays at its projection speed.
On a $v$-$t$ graph zero acceleration is zero gradient, a horizontal line at non-zero $v$. This matches graph Q, not graph R which slopes slightly downward.
Vertically the initial component is zero because projection is horizontal, and the uniform gravitational field gives constant downward acceleration $g$.
With $u = 0$ and $a = g$, $v = u + at$ gives $v = gt$, so vertical speed grows linearly from the origin with constant gradient $g$.
On a $v$-$t$ graph this is a straight line through $(0,0)$, which is graph P. Graph S is curved with increasing gradient, so acceleration is not constant.
Horizontal Q with vertical P is the pairing listed. This is option A.

A.explanation: Graph Q shows constant non-zero $v$ for horizontal motion with no acceleration, and graph P shows $v$ starting at zero and increasing linearly for vertical fall with constant $g$.

B.explanation: Graph Q correctly shows constant horizontal velocity, but graph S is curved with increasing gradient and does not show the constant acceleration $a = g$ of vertical fall.

C.explanation: Graph P correctly shows vertical velocity $v = gt$ from zero, but graph R shows decreasing $v$ whereas horizontal velocity stays constant.

D.explanation: Graph R shows a slightly decreasing $v$ and graph S shows accelerating $v$ with increasing gradient, neither of which matches constant horizontal velocity and uniformly accelerated vertical velocity.
